Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, please press star then the number one on your touchtone phone. We will take questions in the order they are received. Our instructions will be repeated at the conclusion of the prepared remarks. I would now like to turn the conference over to Jennifer Brooks, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Brooks:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me this morning are James Whitaker, our Chief Executive Officer; Robert Kline, our Chief Financial Officer; Emily Novak, our Chief Risk Officer; and Thomas Reilly, our Chief Credit Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to James Whitaker.

James Whitaker:
Thank you, Jennifer, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered strong performance in the third quarter, driven by our commitment to customer service and operational excellence.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on growing our core businesses, investing in technology and innovation, managing risk effectively, optimizing our capital allocation, and enhancing our employee engagement.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. On technology investments, we're seeing transformative efficiency gains from our cloud migrations, AI deployments, and automation efforts, which have improved our efficiency ratio significantly. Regarding asset sensitivity, our modestly positive gap has supported NII growth amid rising rates, with robust hedging in place. We've built reserves prudently to address CRE and consumer pressures, maintaining strong coverage ratios. Deposit growth has been solid across transactional, savings, and time categories, bolstering our funding mix. Finally, our provision reflects forward-looking CECL modeling amid macro uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Robert Kline to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, James, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $1.25 billion for the third quarter, or $2.85 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% year-over-year due to robust loan growth and an expanded net interest margin of 3.45%. Non-interest income rose 6% to $850 million, supported by fee income from payments and wealth management. Key performance indicators include an efficiency ratio of 54%, return on equity of 13.2%, and CET1 capital of 12.8%. We are confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me dive deeper into some of these areas starting with our technology investments and their impact on efficiency. In this competitive landscape, with fintech challengers like Chime and Revolut alongside Big Tech entrants such as Apple and Google, we've made technology a cornerstone for controlling costs, driving revenues, and strengthening risk controls. Over the last two years, we've committed around $750 million to focused tech projects—about 12% of non-interest expenses—generating strong returns via tangible productivity improvements.

Our cloud migration stands out: we've moved 75% of core banking operations to a hybrid setup using AWS for transaction heavy-lifting and Azure for AI and machine learning tasks. This cut data center costs by 28%, saving $120 million yearly, and boosted uptime to 99.99%, avoiding the multimillion-dollar hits from peer outages. Consequently, our efficiency ratio dropped to 54% this quarter from 61% in Q3 2022, beating the S&P Global industry average of 58%. Non-interest expenses grew only 2.1% year-over-year, below the expected 4-5%.

AI and ML have revolutionized operations. Generative AI tools, customized with our data much like JPMorgan's IndexGPT, now handle customer service, underwriting, and fraud. Our app-based chatbot, serving 85 million active global users, resolves 65% of basic queries, slashing call center use by 40% and saving $85 million in staff costs. For small business loans, ML speeds approvals from five days to two hours, lifting volumes 18% without added personnel. Fraud detection using graph neural networks caught $250 million in suspicious activity in Q3, up 35% from old systems, countering FBI-noted synthetic identity fraud.

Robotic process automation and low-code tools like UiPath and Mendix enable straight-through processing. In payments, 70% of reconciliations in our correspondent banking are automated, reducing costs 22% and backing 15% higher cross-border volumes despite currency swings—key as we lead in Swift's ISO 20022 shift.

These efforts vary by region. In North America, with 92% digital transactions in U.S. retail, API ties to Plaid and Finicity personalize offers, growing deposits 12% through neobroker partnerships like Robinhood. Digital customer costs fell 19% to $45 from $120 for branches. Europe's PSD2 and PSD3 push led to a $150 million Open Banking Platform for 500+ partners, complying with GDPR while adding €2.5 billion in fees from data and white-labeling; efficiency rose 16%, topping Eurozone norms where tech-to-revenue is 8-10%. In Asia-Pacific, our super-app akin to WeChat Pay and Grab, via Tencent Cloud, holds 45% Southeast Asia remittance share, cutting costs 25% with blockchain for CBDC links per Singapore's MAS pilots; NIM grew 25 basis points to 3.45% via AI deposit pricing, netting $15 billion in cheap funds.

These are ongoing: we aim for sub-50% efficiency by 2025 end with $300 million more capex on quantum-secure cyber defenses—vital amid 300% ransomware jumps per Chainalysis—and edge computing for treasury. Our 3.2x ROI on tech (three-year NPV savings) outshines Wells Fargo's 20% of $6 billion program or HSBC's $2 billion digital push. With CET1 at 12.8%, we'll ramp gen AI in CIB for 10% better cross-sell. Challenges like EU AI Act bias rules and talent gaps are met with 25% tech staff growth to 8,000 via Coursera training.

In short, tech is propelling us ahead in banking efficiency for lasting outperformance.

Shifting to our deposit franchise, the foundation of our funding. Total deposits hit $285 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year versus FDIC's 4.8% industry mark, and 1.1% quarter-over-quarter despite seasonal flows. This keeps our loan-to-deposit ratio at 82%, enabling lending without heavy wholesale dependence.

Transactional deposits—demand and NOW accounts—at 48% of mix, up from 46%, grew 4.5% to $137 billion via SMB relationship banking. Southeast hubs like Atlanta and Charlotte added 22% inflows through treasury tools akin to JPMorgan's Chase Connect. Despite fintech rivals like Chime, betas stay low at 15 basis points since March 2022 hikes. Our "Deposit Lock-In" uses AI scoring for loan-linked sweeps, boosting top SMB retention 10%.

Savings—money markets and high-yield—at 35%, up from 32%, jumped 12.8% to $100 billion via Horizon YieldBoost at 4.75% APY, like Ally's amid curve inversion. Midwest Ohio/Indiana led with 35% growth as inflation shifts from CDs. Betas at 65% match industry but we cap at 55% aggregate via real-time algorithms tied to FHLB rates. "Savings Ladders" in our app—automated 3/6/12-month buckets—lifted inflows 15%, stabilizing NIM at 3.45% with 10-15 bps Q4 gain eyed.

Time deposits—CDs/brokered—at 17%, rose 9.1% to $48 billion, though quarterly at 0.8% from maturing jumbos. 5-month specials at 5.10% like Marcus drew uptake; Texas Dallas expansion grew them 18% for CRE. We limit brokrogued to 10% avoiding Basel III HQLA hits, favoring retail via geo-ads and CDARS, adding $2.5 billion insured. Shifting to short-term to align 2.8-year liability duration.

Our approach: digital via Horizon One app (40% new deposits) with Zelle, round-ups, ML cash tools; $50 million marketing for young depositors (+25% sub-$10k accounts); bi-weekly pricing committee using SNL data. Tailored regionally: Southeast transactional, Midwest savings, Southwest time. 65% core ratio (>90-day stable transactional/savings) guards against fintech and cuts; guide 6-8% full-year growth, mix to 50/35/15, NIM to 3.55%, backing 5.2% ROE and liquidity like post-SVB.

Next, our asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management, key to balance sheet strength post-Fed's 525 bps hikes since March 2022 and inverted curve. Our modest asset sensitivity has aided NIM, but we hedge rate-cut risks.

Gap: $285 billion RSA (62% earning assets) vs. $240 billion RSL (55% liabilities) in 12 months, positive $45 billion gap. +100 bps shock: +$420 million NII (+2.8%); +200 bps: +$810 million (+5.4%). -100 bps: -$310 million (-2.1%).

EVE: +100 bps hits 3.2% or $1.2 billion, duration gap 0.15 years (assets 3.8, liabilities 3.65) vs. 1.8 years pre-hikes. De-risked $15 billion fixed mortgages via sales/securitizations like Wells/U.S. Bancorp.

NIM up 85 bps to 3.45% on 68% LTD, sticky deposits (non-time beta 35%, CDs 75%). Deposits cost 2.80% from 0.90%; forward curve implies 75 bps Fed cuts by mid-2024. U.S. (80% BS): +$38 billion gap, C&I SOFR+285 bps on $120 billion. Europe: neutral $2 billion, €8 billion payer swaps at 3.50% vs. ECB 4.50%. APAC (12%): slight liability sensitivity hedged with AUD/JPY swaps, EaR down 40%.

Tools: daily VaR/Monte Carlo on Moody's AXIS. Dynamic hedges: $25 billion swaps (80% receive-fixed), futures/swaptions; floors -200 bps NII at -4.1% from -7.2%. ARMs 45% residential (SOFR 6.25%); $10 billion floating notes for CRE. Stresses include bear steeper (NII flat); HTM/AOCI losses $2.1 billion from $4.8 peak, LCR >140%. High-yield savings at 4.75% grew core 8% QoQ, betas 40%.

Asset sensitivity is our edge vs. peers' negative gaps; 92% retail mix aids pricing. Target +100 bps NII beta 2.5-3.0% to 2025 with two 25 bps cuts. Embedded cards with Affirm diversify. Risks: CRE duration, but 65% LTV, PD <1.5%.

Delivered $1.2 billion extra NII YTD, hedged for FOMC paths.

Now to credit reserves—provision, ALLL under CECL U.S./IFRS 9 international. Q3 $285 million build vs. Q2 $210 million release, near $270 million consensus. Prudent for inflation, CRE from Fed cuts delay.

CECL: base 65%, adverse 25%, severe 10% weights. Base: GDP 1.8% 2025, unemployment 4.3%, 75 bps cuts. Tilted adverse on:

CRE $45 billion (office 28%, multi 42%): $42 million NCOs +15% QoQ; vacancies 19.5% CBRE, sunbelt shifts downgrade NYC/SF; PD +20-25 bps higher-for-longer.

Consumer $120 billion cards/auto: delinq 2.1% from 1.9%, 5.5% card util; like Cap One/Discover subprime seasoning.

CIB $250 billion: leveraged/middle-market criticized +8% to $4.2 billion, LGD to 45% retail/energy.

Release in mortgages $15 billion, losses 0.45% FHFA stable.

Regions: U.S. 72% loans 80% build, Northeast CRE; Europe 15% $20 million release ECB/German industrials; APAC 13% neutral, Singapore trade vs. China property $2.8 billion hedged NPL sales.

ALLL $12.7 billion +$285 million: 1.47% loans $863 billion (from 1.42%, target 1.3-1.5%; JPM 1.35%, BAC 1.52%). NPLs $4.45 billion 0.52% coverage 285% (ex-CRE 320%); criticized 62% from 58%; NCO $195 million 23 bps coverage 4.2x.

Trends: delinq -5 bps YoY retail; CRE NCOs peak Q1 down post $1.2 billion sales.

Enhancements: GenAI Moody's alt data (CRE satellite, social sentiment) accuracy +12%, volatility -3-5 bps; climate overlays Fed SR 22-7 $15 million; 2023-24 vintages PD -20%, DSCR 1.25x CRE.

Derisked $3.5 billion high-LGD CRE syndications/Blackstone JV office-resi. CET1 12.1% for wealth/green growth.

Q4 PCL $200-300 million no recession; fortress coverage outperforms soft landing/downturn.

Relatedly, provision for credit losses at $450 million, +15% QoQ from $390 million, flat YoY $452 million on $450 billion loans. ACL $12.5 billion, 2.8% coverage vs. peer 2.4% FDIC, +10 bps.

Drivers:

Macro 40% $180 million: base/adverse/severe 60/30/10 Moody's/Fed; GDP 1.8%, unemp 4.3%, 10yr 4.2%, inflation 3.1%; CRE vac 20.1% CBRE/NYCB-like; MBS prepays slow $85 billion mortgages.

Portfolio/delinq 35% $158 million: C&I 28% delinq 1.2% +25 bps SMB manuf/retail $120 million, PD China trade; CRE 15% $95 million office $18 billion 3.5% from 2.1% multi 0.8%; consumer 40% cards 2.9% <Visa 3.2% autos 1.1% $80 million used car -5% Manheim BNPL Affirm/Klarna; mortgages 17% $55 million jumbo Fannie.

Idiosyncratic 25% $112 million: NCO $320 million 72 bps 2021-22 C&I; recoveries 25 bps; Midwest auto UAW, WC tech VC.

Regions: U.S. 75%, Europe Deutsche JV $60 million ECB German 1.8%, APAC $30 million Singapore/China cool.

Methodology ASC 326: PD logistic 24mo 150+ vars unemp/CRE cap/Conf Board, 2023 PD -15%; LGD DCF coll haircut office 40% multi 25% 2008 stress; EAD behavioral Basel; weighting qualitative geo Red Sea +10 bps shipping.

Tech: $25 million Palantir NLP transcripts/satellite Orbital, errors -18%; Snowflake CECL weekly QT $95B/mo.

CET1 11.8% +220 bps; derisk office $2B sales/synd, MBS/Treas, AI SMB PD -20 bps, $10B SOFR swaps.

Q4 $420-470 million no recession, upside CRE reviews; ahead peers WFC/PNC coverage.

Emily Novak:
Thank you, Robert. As Chief Risk Officer, I would like to briefly discuss our risk management framework. We continue to prioritize proactive risk identification and mitigation. Our key focus areas include interest rate volatility and credit deterioration in CRE and consumer segments, informed by our advanced modeling and hedging. We remain vigilant in monitoring emerging risks like cyber threats and geopolitical tensions, adapting strategies with daily VaR and stress tests to ensure resilience.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Mike Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Lopez:
Good morning, team. Can you provide more detail on your technology investments and the ROI you're seeing there?

James Whitaker:
Thanks for the question, Mike. Our $750 million over two years is delivering outsized returns, with efficiency ratio compression to 54%, $120 million annual cloud savings, $85 million AI labor cuts, and fraud prevention gains. Regional tailoring—in North America personalization, Europe open banking €2.5 billion fees, APAC super-app cost drops—positions us for sub-50% efficiency by 2025, with 3.2x ROI tracking peers favorably.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Thanks. What are your expectations for deposit growth and mix in a potential rate-cutting environment?

Robert Kline:
Great question, Sarah. We guide 6-8% full-year growth to $285 billion-plus, mix shifting to 50/35/15 transactional/savings/time. Core 65% sticky with low betas—transactional 15 bps, savings 55% aggregate. Strategies like AI sweeps, YieldBoost 4.75%, short-term CDs, digital app 40% inflows, and regional focus sustain this even with cuts, supporting NIM to 3.55% and healthy LTD.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you comment on the credit quality of your CRE portfolio?

Thomas Reilly:
Absolutely, David. CRE at $45 billion sees office stress with 3.5% delinqs and $42 million Q3 NCOs amid 19.5-20.1% vacancies, but multi steady at 0.8%. Coverage robust: ALLL 1.47% loans, 285% NPLs. Derisking $3.5-5 billion sales/syndications/JVs, tightened DSCR 1.25x, PD uplifts modeled. NCOs trending down post-peak, vintages improving; positioned well with CET1 buffer.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to James Whitaker for any closing remarks.

James Whitaker:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
